Former FBI Officials Charged With Lying To Congress About Hunter Biden Probes

'When senior officials entrusted with safeguarding our nation’s security choose deception over duty, they undermine the very institutions they swore to uphold.'

Actual Article Body:
‘When senior officials entrusted with safeguarding our nation’s security choose deception over duty, they undermine the very institutions they swore to uphold.’

Two former FBI officials have been charged with lying to Congress about their roles in the agency’s Hunter Biden probes, federal authorities announced Friday.

“Lying to Congress by anyone strikes at the heart of our democratic system­­ but when senior FBI agents lie to Congress believing they are above the law, it’s time to bring the hammer of justice down on them,” U.S. Attorney for the District of Columbia Jeanine Pirro said in a statement announcing the indictment. “When senior officials entrusted with safeguarding our nation’s security choose deception over duty, they undermine the very institutions they swore to uphold. Today’s action makes clear that no one is above the law, and we will hold accountable all who obstruct the truth.”

According to FBI Director Kash Patel, federal authorities took former FBI officials Nikki Floris and Bradley Benavides into custody on Friday morning. Both have been charged for allegedly lying to Congress in 2023 about their roles in the FBI’s since-dissolved Foreign Influence Task Force (FITF).

Sen. Chuck Grassley, R-Iowa, revealed in October 2023 how the task force “used a sham assessment opened by FBI headquarters to cull reporting from confidential human sources (CHS) throughout the country related to the Biden family and then falsely brand the intelligence as ‘foreign disinformation,'” as The Federalist’s Margot Cleveland reported. The news came a year after Grassley revealed whistleblower allegations that the Christopher Wray-led FBI “developed information in 2020 about Hunter Biden’s criminal financial and related activity but ultimately shut it down based on false assertions that it was subject to foreign disinformation.”

Floris — who once bragged about “running a shadow government across the FBI” — served as the FITF’s deputy assistant director from mid-2019 through mid-2022, according to Patel. Benavides was the task force’s section chief from mid-2019 through the 2020 election.

According to the newly released criminal complaint, both former officials “knowingly and willfully provided materially false information about their awareness of and involvement in the FBI’s investigations into Hunter Biden” when testifying before Congress in 2023. Pirro’s office alleged that their sworn statements “were contradicted by documentary evidence, communications, and witness accounts and concerned matters directly relevant to the congressional investigation.”

“The evidence further establishes probable cause to believe that FLORIS and BENAVIDES made these statements for the purpose of concealing FITF’s engagement with and communications about the Hunter Biden investigations and impeding the congressional investigation,” the complaint reads. “Accordingly, there is probable cause to believe that FLORIS and BENAVIDES violated 18 U.S.C. § 1001(a)(2), by knowingly and willfully making materially false statements in a matter within the jurisdiction of the legislative branch.”

Hunter Biden was convicted on federal charges related to an unlawful gun purchase and later pled guilty to several tax offenses in 2024, although the indictments were largely seen as a cover for obfuscating Joe Biden’s role in the Biden family business. The younger Biden received a sweeping pardon from his father during the latter’s final days in office.

As described by Pirro’s office, Floris testified to Congress “that she had no involvement in the Hunter Biden investigations” and that “she knew nothing” about Hunter’s infamous laptop. According to the feds, however, Floris “was in frequent communication with the case team for over a year during which she both sent and received information about Hunter Biden,” and “coordinated the FBI’s response to news articles about the laptop in real time.”

These and other “knowing, willful, and materially false statements hindered a duly convened Congressional committee from exercising oversight of the Executive Branch,” the complaint reads.

Pirro’s office alleged that Benavides’ testimony followed a similar pattern. The federal agency contended, for example, that the then-FBI official “testified that he knew about” the New York Post’s 2020 report on Hunter’s laptop regarding Hunter “[o]nly in the—from the prep material,” despite allegedly “extensively discuss[ing] the laptop story the day it broke.”

The complaint includes additional examples of what the U.S. Attorney’s Office for D.C. alleges amount to perjury by Floris and Benavides.

WASHINGTON — Two former FBI officials were charged on Friday with lying to Congress about their involvement in investigating Hunter Biden’s laptop in the run-up to the 2020 presidential election, the latest in a series of splashy and politically charged actions the Justice Department has undertaken ahead of next month’s midterm contests.

Nikki Floris and Bradley Benavides, former top leaders of a since-disbanded task force set up to counter foreign election interference, surrendered to authorities and made their first appearance in federal court in Washington, where their lawyers pressed for a speedy hearing at which they could contest the allegations against them.

The prosecution, a rare Department of Justice criminal case against a former employee, revisits a tangled and peculiar saga that roiled the final weeks of the 2020 race. It also comes amid a broader, backward-looking effort by FBI Director Kash Patel, who before taking over the nation’s premier law enforcement agency was a harsh critic of it, to scrutinize high-profile episodes from the bureau’s recent past that for years have animated President Donald Trump’s conservative base.

Floris’ attorneys called her “a patriot” and said she has “served our nation as a dedicated FBI intelligence officer for nearly 20 years.”

“Yet today, the DOJ has accused her falsely of a crime on the say-so of politicians, not on the facts,” her attorneys said in a statement. “It’s no coincidence the government is filing these nonsense charges now, years later, on the eve of an election.”

The case was filed 10 days before the Nov. 3 elections via criminal complaint, which means prosecutors have not yet presented the case to a grand jury for an indictment. The Justice Department has repeatedly struggled in high-profile cases to convince grand juries in the nation’s capital to return indictments.

During the former FBI employees’ court appearance, both defense attorneys and the judge noted the unusual move to charge the case through a criminal complaint, which is more often used by prosecutors when they have an urgent need to take people into custody because, for example, they present a danger or a risk of flight.

U.S. Magistrate Judge Zia Faruqui remarked that it is “rare that we have charges this old coming in this nature.” Faruqui set a preliminary hearing for next Tuesday over the objections of prosecutors, who pushed for more time given what the judge described as the “sword of Damocles” hanging over the defendants’ head.

The revelation of the laptop’s existence in October 2020 injected a thorny storyline in the race between Trump, the Republican incumbent, and Biden’s father, Joe Biden, Trump’s Democratic challenger, who went on to win the race.

The complaint aims to build on longstanding congressional Republican complaints about the FBI’s handling of the laptop, including allegations that the bureau was not forthcoming to the public about its conclusion that the materials on it — including emails that showed discussions of the younger Biden’s foreign business dealings — were authentic and not the product of Russian disinformation.

The laptop’s contents were publicized by the New York Post, which said it had obtained from Trump ally Rudy Giuliani a hard drive of a computer dropped off by Hunter Biden at a Wilmington, Delaware, repair shop about a year earlier.

The curious circumstances of the laptop’s discovery raised concerns among Democrats and former intelligence officials about the possibility of Russian disinformation, particularly at a time when the Trump administration’s own intelligence community had assessed that Russia was attempting to interfere on Trump’s behalf in the election and as Giuliani had traveled abroad looking for dirt on the Bidens. Dozens of former U.S. intelligence officials signed a letter saying that the laptop bore the hallmarks of an “information campaign.”

But Trump’s then-director of national intelligence, John Ratcliffe, said in a letter to Congress that there was no proof foreign actors had anything to do with Hunter Biden’s laptop. The FBI under then-Director Chris Wray subsequently backed up that assessment.

Hunter Biden was subsequently charged with, and convicted of, gun and tax offenses during his father’s administration. Joe Biden pardoned him in his final weeks in office.

The complaint alleges that in their capacity as leaders of the Foreign Influence Task Force, Floris and Benavides were engaged in the investigations into Hunter Biden, and that Biden was a recurring subject at FITF meetings. Yet, the complaint says, both downplayed their firsthand knowledge of the laptop or involvement in investigations during 2023 congressional testimony. It accuses Benavides of making a false statement by telling lawmakers that he learned through Wikipedia that the FBI was in possession of the laptop.

“Lying to Congress by senior FBI officials strikes at the heart of our system. No one is above the law,” Patel said.

The case brings renewed attention to the work of the task force, which was established in the first Trump administration to police influence campaigns staged by Russia and other nations aimed at sowing discord, undermining democracy and spreading disinformation. The task force became a magnet of congressional Republican criticism during the Biden investigation and was disbanded in February 2025 by then-Attorney General Pam Bondi in one of her first acts on the job.

As FBI director, Patel has presided over widespread firings of agents who were involved in investigations of Trump or who are perceived as being against the Republican administration’s agenda.

He has also focused attention on years-old investigations like the Hunter Biden one that occurred before he became director and that have been the subject of grievances and complaints by Trump allies.

The Justice Department historically looks to avoid public and overt investigative acts in the direct lead-up to an election that involve candidates or that risk influencing an outcome. But officials in the last two weeks have made a series of bold moves in cases with political undertones, including a search of Democratic Rep. Ilhan Omar’s house in an immigration fraud investigation and a corruption indictment unsealed Thursday against powerful Democratic Virginia state Sen. L. Louise Lucas.

Omar and Lucas are both Trump critics. Omar, who’s from Minnesota, has called the search of her Washington home an “attempt to target political enemies and weaponize federal law enforcement.” Lucas has said she won’t be intimidated or bullied by the federal government in its case against her and “will not back down.”

Collingwood has won just one game out of 11 this season. (Getty: Matt Roberts/AFL Photos)

Former AFLW player and coach Lauren Arnell has slammed the standard of Collingwood, while emphasising the responsibility of coaches to "put on a show" to grow the game.

The Magpies slumped to a new low on Friday night after failing to kick a single goal against Port Adelaide.

The 48-point defeat to the Power was the club's 10th loss this season out of 11 games. Under head coach Sam Wright, the Magpies have won just five games since the start of 2024.

"Overall, it was not the best standard of AFLW football that we would expect to see at this point of season 11," Arnell said on ABC Radio.

"Ash Centra was one of the first to walk off the ground in tears right in front of us. Totally fair. I would probably be about the same level."

Sam Wright took over as head coach at the end of 2023 and has struggled to get wins on the board since. (Getty: Mark Brake)

The pioneer of women's football and former captain of Carlton said while the AFLW continued to play 16 a side in venues open to conditions, unlike protected stadiums the MCG, Perth Stadium and Docklands in the men's game, if teams did not have high skill levels or offensive systems, they would not be able to put goals on the board.

"If you're Sam Wright, you've made some clear decisions where you want to play plus two behind the ball for a lot of the game. And my personal belief is that if you do that in AFLW, you're giving up score, and that's what we saw again tonight," Arnell said.

"And having coached against Collingwood in 2024, we beat them here at Alberton, and it was quite frustrating as a coach and someone who's been invested in women's sport and AFLW for a period of time, [as] you know that broadcast relies on high scoring.

"People who forever criticise AFLW as a sport, or a league, will always point to the lack of score and short quarters … and I'm a firm non-believer in heavy defensive systems for all of those reasons, not just because you can't score, but because we have a responsibility if you're coaching to grow the game and put on a show."

Ruby Schleicher, captain of Collingwood, will leave the Magpies at the end of the AFLW season. (Getty: Martin Keep)

Last week, Collingwood CEO Craig Kelly fronted the AFLW playing group after media reports of player unrest and concerns with the operation of the women's program.

Kelly told News Corp that when AFLW was to be introduced in 2017, Collingwood put its hand up to be an inaugural club, but now he often wondered if the Magpies would have been better off waiting to enter the women's competition at a later date.

He conceded being a foundation AFLW club might have been a mistake, while ruling out any prospect of an independent review into the women's program, which other struggling clubs have done, such as Carlton in 2023, Richmond in 2025 and St Kilda following this season.

Former player and coach Lauren Arnell slams non-offensive styles of play in the AFLW. (Getty: Russell Freeman/AFL Photos)

To Arnell, those remarks from Kelly screamed a lack of understanding between the executive and the playing cohort.

"That statement just immediately tells me you have never sat down with enough of your women's players and even asked them questions of their perspective and where they've come from," Arnell said.

"Like you've got no understanding of your playing group and potentially your coaching group."

Despite being one of the biggest sporting clubs in Victoria, Collingwood players are reported to feel behind local rivals in Melbourne, North Melbourne and Carlton, and are unhappy with multiple aspects of the program, including coaching, high performance and list management.

Collingwood is not alone down the bottom of the ladder, with St Kilda and Essendon also entering round 11 having won only one game this season.

Essendon players have looked frustrated and dejected after losses this season. (Getty: Michael Willson/AFL Photos)

"And I'll guarantee you, off the back of that, there's going to be a lot of movement in the trade period coming up in the next month and a half," Arnell said.

There is an expected player exodus from Collingwood at the season's end, with captain Ruby Schleicher already announcing she'll be leaving to head back to Western Australia. It is reported the West Coast Eagles offered her a four-year deal, while the Magpies' initial offer was a one-year contract extension, then upped to two.

On top of Schleicher, the high-profile players such as Tarni White, Brianna Davey, Sarah Rowe and Lauren Butler are all out of contract at season's end. Vice-captain Jordy Allen tried to exit last trade period for Brisbane but Collingwood blocked her attempts.

"I think the washout of this whole storyline will be well beyond Collingwood, and we're going to see evidence of it across the trade period coming in December, and it will be really clear which players feel like their club's not invested in the environment," Arnell said.

2 ex-FBI officials charged with making false statements about Hunter Biden’s laptop

Two former FBI intelligence officials who specialized in foreign election interference were charged Friday with making false statements about their roles in investigating the origins of Hunter Biden’s laptop in the run-up to the 2020…

WASHINGTON — Two former FBI officials were charged on Friday with lying to Congress about their involvement in investigating Hunter Biden’s laptop in the run-up to the 2020 presidential election, the latest in a series of splashy and politically charged actions the Justice Department has undertaken ahead of next month’s midterm contests.

Nikki Floris and Bradley Benavides, former top leaders of a since-disbanded task force set up to counter foreign election interference, surrendered to authorities and made their first appearance in federal court in Washington, where their lawyers pressed for a speedy hearing at which they could contest the allegations against them.

The prosecution, a rare Department of Justice criminal case against a former employee, revisits a tangled and peculiar saga that roiled the final weeks of the 2020 race. It also comes amid a broader, backward-looking effort by FBI Director Kash Patel, who before taking over the nation’s premier law enforcement agency was a harsh critic of it, to scrutinize high-profile episodes from the bureau’s recent past that for years have animated President Donald Trump’s conservative base.

Floris’ attorneys called her “a patriot” and said she has “served our nation as a dedicated FBI intelligence officer for nearly 20 years.”

“Yet today, the DOJ has accused her falsely of a crime on the say-so of politicians, not on the facts,” her attorneys said in a statement. “It’s no coincidence the government is filing these nonsense charges now, years later, on the eve of an election.”

The case was filed 10 days before the Nov. 3 elections via criminal complaint, which means prosecutors have not yet presented the case to a grand jury for an indictment. The Justice Department has repeatedly struggled in high-profile cases to convince grand juries in the nation’s capital to return indictments.

During the former FBI employees’ court appearance, both defense attorneys and the judge noted the unusual move to charge the case through a criminal complaint, which is more often used by prosecutors when they have an urgent need to take people into custody because, for example, they present a danger or a risk of flight.

U.S. Magistrate Judge Zia Faruqui remarked that it is “rare that we have charges this old coming in this nature.” Faruqui set a preliminary hearing for next Tuesday over the objections of prosecutors, who pushed for more time given what the judge described as the “sword of Damocles” hanging over the defendants’ head.

The revelation of the laptop’s existence in October 2020 injected a thorny storyline in the race between Trump, the Republican incumbent, and Biden’s father, Joe Biden, Trump’s Democratic challenger, who went on to win the race.

The complaint aims to build on longstanding congressional Republican complaints about the FBI’s handling of the laptop, including allegations that the bureau was not forthcoming to the public about its conclusion that the materials on it — including emails that showed discussions of the younger Biden’s foreign business dealings — were authentic and not the product of Russian disinformation.

The laptop’s contents were publicized by the New York Post, which said it had obtained from Trump ally Rudy Giuliani a hard drive of a computer dropped off by Hunter Biden at a Wilmington, Delaware, repair shop about a year earlier.

The curious circumstances of the laptop’s discovery raised concerns among Democrats and former intelligence officials about the possibility of Russian disinformation, particularly at a time when the Trump administration’s own intelligence community had assessed that Russia was attempting to interfere on Trump’s behalf in the election and as Giuliani had traveled abroad looking for dirt on the Bidens. Dozens of former U.S. intelligence officials signed a letter saying that the laptop bore the hallmarks of an “information campaign.”

But Trump’s then-director of national intelligence, John Ratcliffe, said in a letter to Congress that there was no proof foreign actors had anything to do with Hunter Biden’s laptop. The FBI under then-Director Chris Wray subsequently backed up that assessment.

Hunter Biden was subsequently charged with, and convicted of, gun and tax offenses during his father’s administration. Joe Biden pardoned him in his final weeks in office.

The complaint alleges that in their capacity as leaders of the Foreign Influence Task Force, Floris and Benavides were engaged in the investigations into Hunter Biden, and that Biden was a recurring subject at FITF meetings. Yet, the complaint says, both downplayed their firsthand knowledge of the laptop or involvement in investigations during 2023 congressional testimony. It accuses Benavides of making a false statement by telling lawmakers that he learned through Wikipedia that the FBI was in possession of the laptop.

“Lying to Congress by senior FBI officials strikes at the heart of our system. No one is above the law,” Patel said.

The case brings renewed attention to the work of the task force, which was established in the first Trump administration to police influence campaigns staged by Russia and other nations aimed at sowing discord, undermining democracy and spreading disinformation. The task force became a magnet of congressional Republican criticism during the Biden investigation and was disbanded in February 2025 by then-Attorney General Pam Bondi in one of her first acts on the job.

As FBI director, Patel has presided over widespread firings of agents who were involved in investigations of Trump or who are perceived as being against the Republican administration’s agenda.

He has also focused attention on years-old investigations like the Hunter Biden one that occurred before he became director and that have been the subject of grievances and complaints by Trump allies.

The Justice Department historically looks to avoid public and overt investigative acts in the direct lead-up to an election that involve candidates or that risk influencing an outcome. But officials in the last two weeks have made a series of bold moves in cases with political undertones, including a search of Democratic Rep. Ilhan Omar’s house in an immigration fraud investigation and a corruption indictment unsealed Thursday against powerful Democratic Virginia state Sen. L. Louise Lucas.

Omar and Lucas are both Trump critics. Omar, who’s from Minnesota, has called the search of her Washington home an “attempt to target political enemies and weaponize federal law enforcement.” Lucas has said she won’t be intimidated or bullied by the federal government in its case against her and “will not back down.”

Former AFLW player and coach Lauren Arnell has slammed the standard of Collingwood, while emphasising the responsibility of coaches to "put on a show" to grow the game.

The Magpies slumped to a new low on Friday night after failing to kick a single goal against Port Adelaide.

The 48-point defeat to the Power was the club's 10th loss this season out of 11 games. Under head coach Sam Wright, the Magpies have won just five games since the start of 2024.

"Overall, it was not the best standard of AFLW football that we would expect to see at this point of season 11," Arnell said on ABC Radio.

"Ash Centra was one of the first to walk off the ground in tears right in front of us. Totally fair. I would probably be about the same level."

Sam Wright took over as head coach at the end of 2023 and has struggled to get wins on the board since. (Getty: Mark Brake)

The pioneer of women's football and former captain of Carlton said while the AFLW continued to play 16 a side in venues open to conditions, unlike protected stadiums the MCG, Perth Stadium and Docklands in the men's game, if teams did not have high skill levels or offensive systems, they would not be able to put goals on the board.

"If you're Sam Wright, you've made some clear decisions where you want to play plus two behind the ball for a lot of the game. And my personal belief is that if you do that in AFLW, you're giving up score, and that's what we saw again tonight," Arnell said.

"And having coached against Collingwood in 2024, we beat them here at Alberton, and it was quite frustrating as a coach and someone who's been invested in women's sport and AFLW for a period of time, [as] you know that broadcast relies on high scoring.

"People who forever criticise AFLW as a sport, or a league, will always point to the lack of score and short quarters … and I'm a firm non-believer in heavy defensive systems for all of those reasons, not just because you can't score, but because we have a responsibility if you're coaching to grow the game and put on a show."

Ruby Schleicher, captain of Collingwood, will leave the Magpies at the end of the AFLW season. (Getty: Martin Keep)

Last week, Collingwood CEO Craig Kelly fronted the AFLW playing group after media reports of player unrest and concerns with the operation of the women's program.

Kelly told News Corp that when AFLW was to be introduced in 2017, Collingwood put its hand up to be an inaugural club, but now he often wondered if the Magpies would have been better off waiting to enter the women's competition at a later date.

He conceded being a foundation AFLW club might have been a mistake, while ruling out any prospect of an independent review into the women's program, which other struggling clubs have done, such as Carlton in 2023, Richmond in 2025 and St Kilda following this season.

Former player and coach Lauren Arnell slams non-offensive styles of play in the AFLW. (Getty: Russell Freeman/AFL Photos)

To Arnell, those remarks from Kelly screamed a lack of understanding between the executive and the playing cohort.

"That statement just immediately tells me you have never sat down with enough of your women's players and even asked them questions of their perspective and where they've come from," Arnell said.

"Like you've got no understanding of your playing group and potentially your coaching group."

Despite being one of the biggest sporting clubs in Victoria, Collingwood players are reported to feel behind local rivals in Melbourne, North Melbourne and Carlton, and are unhappy with multiple aspects of the program, including coaching, high performance and list management.

Collingwood is not alone down the bottom of the ladder, with St Kilda and Essendon also entering round 11 having won only one game this season.

Essendon players have looked frustrated and dejected after losses this season. (Getty: Michael Willson/AFL Photos)

"And I'll guarantee you, off the back of that, there's going to be a lot of movement in the trade period coming up in the next month and a half," Arnell said.

There is an expected player exodus from Collingwood at the season's end, with captain Ruby Schleicher already announcing she'll be leaving to head back to Western Australia. It is reported the West Coast Eagles offered her a four-year deal, while the Magpies' initial offer was a one-year contract extension, then upped to two.

On top of Schleicher, the high-profile players such as Tarni White, Brianna Davey, Sarah Rowe and Lauren Butler are all out of contract at season's end. Vice-captain Jordy Allen tried to exit last trade period for Brisbane but Collingwood blocked her attempts.

"I think the washout of this whole storyline will be well beyond Collingwood, and we're going to see evidence of it across the trade period coming in December, and it will be really clear which players feel like their club's not invested in the environment," Arnell said.
